title: Fuzzy schema adaptor and user-facing repair suggestion playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a pragmatic "fuzzy" schema adaptor layer for function/tool call parameter validation that: 1) allows safe but explainable coercions, 2) emits rich repair suggestions when inputs violate schemas, and 3) negotiates schema version compatibility with confidence scores. The adaptor aims to reduce application-level errors caused by small format mismatches while preserving deterministic fallback behavior for strict tenants.
motivation: Production callers (webhooks, user-typed prompts, legacy SDKs) often send near-correct payloads that fail strict JSON schema validation. Each failure can cascade into poor user experience and increased engineering toil. Existing work has focused on strict validation + humanized errors; this ticket designs an intermediate 'fuzzy' layer that prefers safe repairs and actionable diagnostics before returning fatal errors.
background: Related internal tickets enumerate error taxonomies and validation strategies (see dependencies). Design review recommended a single opt-in 'fuzzy_mode' per route and stable, auditable transformations. Legal and compliance asked that no silent PII transformations occur — every coercion must be logged and reversible.
design_decisions: 1) Make fuzzy behavior opt-in via a route-level flag (fuzzy_mode: "suggest" | "coerce" | "strict"). 2) Any coercion produces structured diagnostics with 'confidence' and 'transform_id' for auditability. 3) Keep canonical validation pipeline: parse -> shape-check -> fuzzy-adapt -> full-validate -> emit diagnostics or accept. 4) Do not auto-coerce for fields labelled 'sensitive' in schema without explicit customer opt-in.
schema_format_examples:
Example compact param manifest (shorthand supported by adaptor):

{
  "user_id": "int|min=1|required",
  "timeout_ms": "int|coerce_from_str|default=3000",
  "metadata": "json|allow_stringified|max_size=10240",
  "mode": "enum[fast,accurate]|default=accurate",
  "note": "string|nullable|fuzzy_text_fix:normalize_whitespace,trim"
}

This shorthand translates to a full JSON Schema with annotations: coerce rules, fuzzy hints, and sensitivity flags.
validation_flow: 1) Raw payload received. 2) Parse JSON; parse errors -> return E_PARSE with pointer and first-byte offset. 3) Quick shape-check: detect missing/extra keys -> if fuzzy_mode!=strict then attempt key-matching heuristics (case-insensitive, hyphen/underscore) and propose repairs. 4) Field-level fuzzy checks: type mismatch -> attempt ordered coercions (string->int, stringified-json->object, numeric string -> float) while computing confidence using heuristics (parse success, regex match, token overlap). 5) Apply coercions only if confidence >= route.threshold or mode==coerce. 6) Re-run strict schema validate; if still failing, return structured error with repair suggestions and example payload. 7) Telemetry emitted for each coercion and for every rejected payload.
runtime_behaviour:
- Coercions are idempotent and reversible: each transform gets a transform_id and inverse operation.
- All fuzzy activity is recorded to a per-token audit log (trace id + transform_id + user-visible message).
- For Dedicated/Private customers, fuzzy_mode defaults to strict unless explicitly enabled by tenant config.
- In streaming/generative flows, the adaptor can operate on partial parameter sets; streaming tokens are buffered until a safe parse boundary is reached.
- When interacting with function/tool calling in the runtime, the adaptor attaches diagnostics to the function call metadata so downstream handlers can decide to accept, reject, or prompt user verification.
error_code_table:
E_PARSE: Malformed JSON input; include byte offset and snippet.
E_SHAPE_MISMATCH: Top-level keys missing/extra; includes proposed key-mapping.
E_TYPE_MISMATCH: Field-level type mismatch after coercion attempts; includes attempted transforms and confidences.
E_SENSITIVE_COERCION_FORBIDDEN: Attempted transform on 'sensitive' field without opt-in.
E_SIZE_LIMIT: Field exceeds size constraints; includes truncated sample for diagnostics.
E_SCHEMA_VERSION_CONFLICT: Consumer submitted older/newer schema version beyond allowed skew; includes negotiation suggestions.
E_FUZZY_REJECTED: Coercions failed confidence threshold; includes repair suggestions and example corrected payload.
user_friendly_messages: Where possible return both machine code and human message. Example: {code: E_TYPE_MISMATCH, message: 'timeout_ms was a string ("3000ms") — converted to 3000ms with 92% confidence. If this is incorrect, send an integer in milliseconds.'}. Messages must avoid leaking internal stack traces and should include a one-line remediation and a link to a docs page.
telemetry: Emit the following metrics: fuzzy.coercion.count, fuzzy.coercion.success.count, fuzzy.coercion.failure.count, fuzzy.mode.usage{mode}, fuzzy.avg.confidence, validation.latency.p50/95/99, validation.reject.rate. Add logs with structured fields: route, tenant_id, trace_id, transform_id, original_value_excerpt.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement adaptor behind a feature flag per-route. 2) Canary to <internal-apps> with fuzzy_mode=suggest and verbose diagnostics for 2 weeks. 3) If metrics show reduced error rate and acceptable precision, enable fuzzy_mode=coerce for selected non-sensitive routes. 4) Provide tenant opt-out and per-field sensitivity annotations. 5) Ship runtime-1.20 canary, then gradual ramp to hosted in runtime-1.20-patch.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for individual coercion rules and reverse transforms.
- Fuzz tests with corpora of real-world webhook payloads (sanitized) to validate proposed repairs.
- Integration tests for streaming parameter ingestion (partial tokens).
- Load test to measure validation latency at 10k rps.
- End-to-end perf + cost impact analysis to ensure batching and KV cache unaffected.

progress_updates: 2025-02-14: RFC drafted and reviewed with API/Platform leads; concensus to proceed with opt-in model.
2025-02-20: Prototype coercion library (string->int, string->json) implemented and unit-tested; initial fuzz corpus run shows 24% reduction in E_TYPE_MISMATCH for internal webhooks.
2025-02-26: Security review session — agreed no automatic PII normalization; added sensitivity flag to schema manifest. Action: update schema registry to accept sensitivity annotations.
2025-03-04: Feature-flag scaffolding merged; telemetry hooks added. Beginning canary with internal apps next week.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Fuzzy adaptor behind flag and enabled for internal canary routes.
2) No silent coercions — all transforms produce diagnostics and transform_id.
3) Feature reduces top-level validation rejects by >=15% on canary traffic without increasing false-positive repairs beyond 3% (measured by manual triage).
4) Telemetry surfaces required metrics and logs are queryable in console.
5) Documentation and SDK notes published for customers.
open_questions:
- What is the canonical confidence scoring algorithm? (simple heuristics vs small ML model)
- How to represent inverse transforms robustly for nested/complex structures?
- Should we allow tenant-level override of allowed transforms for Private deployments?
- How to surface repair acceptance to interactive UIs (auto-accept vs explicit confirm)?
next_steps: 1) Finalize confidence scoring design (eng + research). 2) Add sensitivity annotations to schema registry (ENG-47291 follow-up). 3) Start internal canary on 2025-03-11. 4) Prepare docs + migration guide for SDK teams.
